example.title: James H. Lane Ranch, Barn (HABS ID-113-A)

brief: Long gambrel-roofed barn whose ground storey is built of rough dark basalt fieldstone laid with thick pale mortar, with dressed concrete lintels and quoin piers, a row of small square stall windows along each long side and a big central drive opening in the gable end. Above the stone the gambrel gable is sided in vertical boards with a hinged hay door and a small loft window, and the long wood-shingle roof is weathered grey and sagging. The HABS barn has one gable end fallen open; here it is intact but old and patched. Board corral fences and a stock gate run off the corner into dry sagebrush pasture.
